questions.question: In the following table, indicate whether each virus is an RNA or DNA virus and whether it is enveloped (Yes or No). For each virus, name one antiviral with activity against it, if any (Mumps is given as an example). Viruses: Mumps, Measles, Hepatitis B, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), Influenza, Zika, Ebola.
questions.question_raw: In the following table, fill out if the virus is RNA/DNA, and whether it is enveloped or not. For each virus, name one antiviral that has activity against it, if any (Mumps is given as an example). Table columns: Virus, RNA or DNA, Enveloped (Yes or No), Antiviral. Viruses listed: Mumps, Measles, Hepatitis B, EBV, Influenza, Zika, Ebola.

parts.text: Complete the table (RNA/DNA, enveloped Yes/No, one antiviral) for: Mumps, Measles, Hepatitis B, Epstein-Barr virus, Influenza, Zika, Ebola.

parts_raw.text: Fill out the table for RNA/DNA, enveloped status, and antiviral for: Mumps, Measles, Hepatitis B, EBV, Influenza, Zika, Ebola

questions.model_answer:
a) Virus | RNA/DNA | Enveloped | Antiviral
(1) Mumps (example) | RNA | Yes | None (supportive care only)
(2) Measles | RNA | Yes | None approved (ribavirin used off-label in severe/immunocompromised cases)
(3) Hepatitis B | DNA | Yes | Tenofovir or entecavir (nucleos[t]ide analogue); pegylated interferon is an alternative
(4) Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) | DNA | Yes | None of proven clinical benefit (acyclovir/ganciclovir have in vitro activity but do not alter disease)
(5) Influenza | RNA | Yes | Oseltamivir (neuraminidase inhibitor); baloxavir (endonuclease inhibitor) is an alternative
(6) Zika | RNA | Yes | None (no licensed antiviral; supportive care)
(7) Ebola | RNA | Yes | Monoclonal antibodies (atoltivimab/maftivimab/odesivimab [Inmazeb] or ansuvimab [Ebanga]); remdesivir/favipiravir investigational
questions.beyond_mandell: Virus taxonomy/RNA-vs-DNA and envelope status, and the HBV, measles, EBV, Zika and Ebola monoclonal-antibody specifics are standard virology/Mandell species chapters plus FDA/WHO Ebola guidance, not this General Principles chapter.

questions.question: Remdesivir.

parts.text: What is its mechanism of action?
What other two viruses (other than SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV) has it been shown to have activity against in animal studies?

parts_raw.text: What is its mechanism of action?
What other 2 viruses (other than SARS-CoV, and MERS-CoV) has it been shown to have activity in animal studies?

questions.model_answer:
a) Remdesivir is an adenosine nucleotide analogue prodrug; it is metabolized intracellularly to the active triphosphate (GS-441524-TP), which competes with ATP for incorporation by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (nsp12) and causes delayed chain termination of nascent viral RNA, evading proofreading by the nsp14 exonuclease.
b) (1) Ebola virus (filoviruses). (2) Nipah virus (paramyxo/henipavirus). It also has in vitro/animal activity against respiratory syncytial virus.

questions.question: Ebola.

parts.text: Name three places the virus can persist after symptoms resolve.

parts_raw.text: 3 places the virus can persist after symptoms resolve

questions.model_answer:
a) (1) Aqueous/vitreous humor of the eye (persistent uveitis). (2) Cerebrospinal fluid / CNS (late relapsing meningoencephalitis). (3) Semen / testes (persists for many months, enabling sexual transmission).
b) Remdesivir (GS-5734) is a monophosphoramidate nucleotide (adenosine) analog prodrug; intracellularly activated to its triphosphate, it is incorporated by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and causes delayed chain termination, inhibiting viral RNA synthesis.
questions.beyond_mandell: Persistence sites and remdesivir mechanism are not detailed in this Mandell slice (GS-5734 is named only as a therapeutic); mechanism/persistence from UpToDate/product data.
